notable_absence.finding: The page ends with a '## See Also' heading (anchor #see-also) followed by no content at all - an orphaned section with nothing listed beneath it, unusual for a Couchbase reference page (which normally lists 2-4 related pages there). No seeAlso relations were extracted from this page because, aside from same-page anchor jumps (e.g. '[Note](#note-1040)'), there are no structural cross-page markdown links in the entire error-code table.

cross_component_finding: The 5xxx RBAC error codes (5210-5281: 'Unable to find user', 'User ... already exists', 'Role ... requires a keyspace', 'User ... already has role', '... did not have role', 'User ... has no roles. Connecting with this user may not be possible', 'Group ... has no roles') structurally parallel the GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE GROUP/CREATE USER RBAC family already modeled in this registry via grantsRole/revokesRole/assignsRole/assignsToGroup/groupMembersInheritRole and rbac-role:role - this confirms that model extends cleanly into the shared error-code surface, with no new relation shapes needed to describe it. Also present: transaction error codes 17001-17099 (Start/Commit/Rollback Transaction, savepoint-not-defined, transaction timeout/queue-full/cas-mismatch) covering the BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT statement family - but nothing on this page textually links those codes to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction from a prior round); flagging as an open question for whichever batch covers the transaction-statement pages directly, per instructions not to assert a relation without textual evidence.
cross_product_finding: This shared server+Capella reference repeatedly cites Enterprise/Community Edition gates verbatim, apparently ported unchanged from server/ prose: error 17097 'Transactions are not supported in Community Edition'; 20000 'Auto Update Statistics is not supported in Community Edition. It is an enterprise level feature.'; 10100 'Functions of type «type» are only supported in Enterprise Edition.'; 3230 '«feature» is an enterprise level feature.'; and 11011 which tells users to 'add the query_system_catalog role' 'In an EE system' or 'add the administrator role' 'In a CE system'. Capella itself has no Community/Enterprise edition split (per the registry's edition:enterprise/edition:community being server/-only concepts), so this is a distinct-but-related variant of the already-logged docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: that issue is about literal 'Couchbase Server X.Y' version strings, whereas this is about Enterprise/Community *edition* names appearing on a page served to Capella users with no edition concept at all. May warrant its own docs-issue entry in reconciliation rather than being folded into the version-citation one.
